children: Arabica coffee futures on ICE turned higher on Wednesday after earlier slumping to a three-month low, while raw sugar and cocoa prices also rose.
rose 0.4% to $2.7340 per lb by 1338 GMT, rebounding from an earlier three-month low of $2.6975.
* Dealers said certified exchange stocks remain very low despite a modest increase in the last few days.
* Stocks stood at 256,678 bags, as of September 22, up from a 27-year low of 217,646 bags a week ago. At the same time last year stocks stood at 643,341 bags.
* They noted further rains were forecast for parts of Brazil's coffee belt as the outlook for next year's crop remains generally favourable.
gained 0.7% to $3,283 a metric ton after slumping to a 3-1/2 month low of $3,218.
* Dealers said mills in Centre-South Brazil had focused this season on using cane to produce biofuel ethanol rather than sugar, helping reduce supplies of the sweetener.
* The prospect of lower production in Asian producers such as India and Thailand due to an El Nino weather event has also helped underpin the market.

* Dealers said dry conditions in top producer Ivory Coast had added to concerns about the prospects for 2026/27 production, although a large global surplus in 2025/26 has ensured that short-term supplies remain ample.

* Ghana's cocoa production for the 2025/26 season reached about 771,000 metric tons, beating regulator COCOBOD's initial forecast of 650,000 tons, according to a report reviewed by Reuters on Wednesday.
